We build SUMMSCREEN, an abstractive summarization dataset combining TV series transcripts and episode recaps. ... We empirically evaluate several types of methods on SUMMSCREEN. We consider nearest neighbor models, neural abstractive summarization models, and hybrid models.
Abstractive summarization aims to produce a summary that concisely expresses key points of the input document rather than merely extracting pieces of it.

We conduct human evaluations for three models: NNM-t2t, hybrid model, and hybrid model (oracle). To evaluate two key aspects of SUMMSCREEN, namely events and characters relationships, we ask human annotators two questions. The first is "Do the predicates in the generation match the predicates in the reference?" The second is "When multiple characters are mentioned as being related in some way in the generated recap, are those same characters mentioned as being related in some way in the reference?" Ratings are on a 1-5 scale with 5 indicating a perfect match.
